mobile.title: Mobile
mobile.sub: At 720px and below the widgets stack in one column, the queue table drops its secondary columns, and the queue is presented as a card list with expandable rows.
mobile.capDashboard: Dashboard — KPI strip, then feed and streams stacked one column
mobile.capQueue: Queue — table becomes a card list; a row expands in place to reveal progress and actions
mobile.rule1d: One column. Feed, streams, queue and health stack in that order — the queue stays the last full-width block.
mobile.rule2d: Service badge, title, quality and status survive on the collapsed card. The progress column and ETA move into the expanded row.
mobile.rule3d: Collapsed cards are 64px tall so eight rows fit on a 667px viewport. Expanded rows grow to fit; the list never scrolls sideways.
mobile.rule4d: Every control is at least 44×44px. The chevron is the only affordance on a collapsed card.
mobile.rule5d: Five fixed destinations, always visible. The queue badge carries the paused count so the user can judge load without opening it.

states.title: Queue action states
states.sub: The four states every queue action passes through, rendered side by side so the handoff is unambiguous.
states.tableTitle: Action states on a queue row
states.staleBody: The banner is discreet, the data greys out, and actions are disabled until the socket is back. Nothing is deleted — the last known values stay on screen and resume from there.
states.legendIdle: Nothing in flight. The row shows the server state.
states.legendPending: The change is sent. The row is tinted and the action shows a spinner.
states.legendSuccess: The server confirmed. The row settles once, then returns to idle.
states.legendError: The server rejected the change. The row reverts and a toast explains why.
states.specSub: The values below are bound to tokens.css — change the token, not the component.
states.specTypeSub: IBM Plex Sans for UI · IBM Plex Mono for numbers
states.densityBody: Density is a single attribute on the root element. Every table cell, feed row and widget picks up the new row height, padding and type size — no component variant is written for it.
